questions.q: Why is perplexity alone not sufficient to evaluate a compressed model?
options: Perplexity cannot be computed for compressed models
Perplexity measures general language modeling and can stay flat even while a specific downstream task's performance collapses
Perplexity requires labeled task data, which makes it too expensive to run
Perplexity only applies to pruned models, not quantized ones
questions.explain: Perplexity is a cheap, general check, but it can remain nearly unchanged while a model's performance on a specific skill or task quietly degrades, since it doesn't measure task competence directly.

questions.q: What is the main point of pairing quality metrics with cost metrics when evaluating a compression technique?
options: Cost metrics are optional and rarely matter
A compression technique should be judged as a pair — quality retained and cost saved — since 'acceptable loss' depends on what the saved cost is being spent on
Quality metrics are only useful once cost has already dropped to zero
Cost metrics replace the need for any quality evaluation at all
questions.explain: There's no universal threshold for acceptable quality loss — the same accuracy drop can be a bad trade or an easy call depending entirely on what cost savings it unlocks (e.g. fitting on fewer GPUs).

questions.q: According to the lesson's decision framework, which compression lever should typically be tried first?
options: Distillation, because it produces the smallest possible model
Pruning, because it is always hardware-accelerated
Quantization, because it's the cheapest to try and the easiest to reverse
All three should always be applied simultaneously from the start
questions.explain: The lesson recommends quantization first since it's low-effort and easily reversible, adding pruning when hardware supports structured sparsity, and reserving distillation for when a genuinely smaller architecture is needed.

questions.q: Why might a published benchmark score be misleading when evaluating a compressed model for your own product?
options: Published benchmarks are always fabricated
A model can score nearly identically on general benchmarks while degrading on a narrow skill your specific product depends on
Published benchmarks only apply to distilled models
Benchmark scores cannot be reproduced by anyone outside the original research team
questions.explain: General benchmarks can look essentially unchanged after compression while a narrow skill the product actually relies on (e.g. structured output or multi-step reasoning) degrades — which is why an eval set built from real use cases matters.

questions.q: Can quantization, pruning, and distillation be combined on the same model?
options: No, applying more than one technique always corrupts the model
Only quantization and pruning can be combined; distillation is always standalone
Yes — the three techniques stack, since a distilled student model can still be quantized and/or pruned afterward
Combining techniques is theoretically possible but has never been done in practice
questions.explain: The three levers are not mutually exclusive: a distilled model is a normal model afterward and can still be quantized or pruned, and pruned/quantized models can likewise be combined further.
